newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH METAL INDUSTRY SEES IMPROVING 1997 OUTLOOK.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH METAL INDUSTRY SEES IMPROVING 1997 OUTLOOK.

text.p: The cyclical outlook for the Finnish metal, engineering and electrotechnical industry seems slightly better next year than in 1996, and hopes that Finland will join EMU are enhancing sales prospects, the sector lobby said on Wednesday.
The sector's sales volume would increase seven percent this year, the Federation of Metal, Engineering and Electrotechnical Industries (MET) said in a statement.
"We expect that the business cycle will be slightly better next year than during the current one," it said.

"Expectations of (Finnish) EMU membership are stabilising the operating environment of our main branches and are thus improving sales possibilities," MET chairman Krister Ahlstrom said in a separate statement.
In 1995, the value of the Finnish metal industry's output was 154 billion markka and the value of the sector's exports was 82 billion markka.
MET gave the following break-down by main branch of forecast production and export volume growth in 1996 over 1995:
Machinery and metal products -- output volume up 3.5 pct (1995 value FIM 78 billion), export volume up 15 pct (35 bln),
Electric and electrotechnical products -- output volume up 10 percent (51 bln), export volume up 7 pct (35 bln),
Base metals -- output volume up 7 pct (31 bln), export volume up 7 pct (14 bln).
